headline: Trump disowns his own June Iran ceasefire as 'sort of a waste of time' and says Iran 'started the war'
dek: Trump, at a Mississippi campaign rally Monday night, said of the June short ceasefire with Iran: 'We announced a short ceasefire. I didn't like it very much' / 'sort of a waste of time.
sources: Donald Trump, campaign rally, Corinth, Mississippi, Oct 26, via Roya News / NY Post / Press TV / Jordan News / Internewscast carries
fault_line: Strike after the midterms, or was the June ceasefire the peace deal Trump just threw away?

sections.what_happened: Trump, at a Mississippi campaign rally Monday night, said of the June short ceasefire with Iran: 'We announced a short ceasefire. I didn't like it very much' / 'sort of a waste of time. But, you know, you like to listen to professionals.' This reverses his June presentation of the deal as 'a great day for world peace' / 'the beginning of a new golden age in the Middle East'. The June agreement, brokered by Pakistan, collapsed without achieving its objectives, including nuclear talks (Roya/Jordan News). In the same rally Trump said 'We didn't start the war with Iran. Iran started the war with us', claimed Iran developed missiles able to hit US cities ('they'd hit San Diego, they'd hit Los Angeles'), and said the offensive 'should've been done a long time ago' (Press TV, Vietnam.vn). Roya/Jordan News add, from unnamed US officials and informed sources, that a new round of strikes on Iranian sites is imminent with expectations it begins after the Nov 3 midterms; Tehran threatened an 'unexpected' response to any US/Israeli attack, hinting at expanded targets including new US bases and undersea internet cables. SEPARATE, ALREADY-RECORDED CONTEXT (not new): Trump told reporters Saturday he would not hit Iran before the Nov 3 midterms (AP via Ahmedabad Mirror, Oct 26); AJ liveblog Oct 27 notes Trump ruled out attacks before the midterms while military options from low-level to MOAB were presented to him.
sections.what_verified: The rally quote is carried identically by 2 declared-tier families: Roya News English (T3) and Press TV (T3, STATE (IR)). NY Post, Jordan News, Internewscast and Vietnam.vn carry the same quote but have NO declared tier in the registry and are NOT counted. The quote itself is the speaker's own words (primary source = the rally speech), so the wording is high-confidence; the post-midterm strike timing rests on unnamed officials/sources in the same Roya text and is ATTRIBUTED REPORT, not a verified plan.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's 'Iran started the war' reverses the recorded chronology: the US-Israeli 'Epic Fury' campaign opened Feb 28, 2026 (recorded in prior scans; Press TV's own counter-framing cites the Feb 28 opening and the assassination of Ayatollah Khamenei). Trump himself said Saturday he would not strike before the Nov 3 midterms, which sits against the 'imminent after midterms' expectation -- both can be true only if 'imminent' means post-Nov 3. The undersea-cable threat is Tehran rhetoric as reported, not a demonstrated capability.
sections.why_matters: Trump just disowned his own June ceasefire -- 'sort of a waste of time' -- the deal he once called 'a great day for world peace'. Same rally: Iran 'started the war', US missiles talk, and officials whispering post-midterm strikes. The June deal is dead by its own author's mouth.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (rally Mon 2026-10-26 night, Corinth, Mississippi; in no prior scan) -- Trump disowns his own June Iran ceasefire as 'sort of a waste of time' and says Iran 'started the war'; US officials talk post-midterm strikes

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump just disowned his own June ceasefire -- 'sort of a waste of time' -- the deal he once called 'a great day for world peace'. Same rally: Iran 'started the war', US missiles talk, and officials whispering post-midterm strikes. The June deal is dead by its own author's mouth. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Strike after the midterms, or was the June ceasefire the peace deal Trump just threw away?
